---
title: "Setup guide"
---

You'll do your coding in **GitHub Codespaces**: the course's Python setup, running
on GitHub's computers and shown in your web browser. There's nothing to install,
and it works the same on any laptop, a Chromebook, or a campus lab computer.
Do steps 1–5 before the second class session. If you get stuck, see the
[Setup FAQ](setup-faq.qmd).

Prefer a desktop editor or working offline? You can also
[work on your own computer](setup-local.qmd). That's optional, and you can add it
any time.

**Before you start:** an internet connection, a current web browser (Chrome,
Edge, Firefox, or Safari), and your phone for GitHub's sign-in codes.

## One-time setup

1. **GitHub**: the website that stores your course work online. Each student gets a private repository ("repo") there, a folder only you and the instructor can see. New problem sets arrive in it. To hand in work, you use Git to save it to your repo, then submit the link to it in Canvas.
   - Sign up at [github.com](https://github.com) with any username (it doesn't need to be your real name), and add your WSU email to the account.
   - Apply for GitHub Education student benefits: see [Get GitHub student benefits](#student-benefits) below. It takes about 10 minutes, and approval can take a few days, so start in Week 1. Your codespace works while you wait.
   - GitHub will ask you to set up two-factor sign-in. Keep that phone or app handy: you'll need a code when you sign in on a lab computer.
   - Enter your GitHub username in the Canvas "GitHub username" survey, so your course repo can be created.

2. **Accept your repo invitation** from the email GitHub sends you, or at
   `https://github.com/WSU-EconS431/2027sp-<your-username>/invitations`.

3. **Create your codespace.** On your repo's page
   (`https://github.com/WSU-EconS431/2027sp-<your-username>`), click the green
   **Code** button, choose the **Codespaces** tab, and click **Create codespace on
   main**.
   - The first time takes a few minutes while it installs Python and the course
     packages. Then an editor opens in your browser. It's VS Code, the program
     Positron is built on.
   - If it offers to turn on GitHub Copilot or AI code completions, skip it for
     now. AI autocomplete stays off through Week 5 (see [Policies](policies.qmd)).

4. **Check it.** Open a terminal: click the **☰** menu at the top left, then
   **Terminal > New Terminal** (or press **Ctrl+`**). Run:

   ```bash
   uv run python check_setup.py
   ```

   Every line should start with `[OK]`.

5. **Do Lab 1 (lab01)** in class on Thursday of Week 1. In the file list on the left, open
   `lab01/lab01.ipynb`. If the notebook asks you to **Select Kernel** (top right), choose
   **Python Environments**, then the one in `.venv`. Complete it, then:
   - In **Source Control** (the branching icon on the left), type a short
     message such as "Lab 1 done" in the box and click **Commit**. Every commit
     needs a message.
   - Click **Sync Changes** to push it to GitHub. Labs have nothing to submit in Canvas.

6. **Then do Problem Set 1 (probset01),** also already in your repo. It's due Monday of
   Week 2 at 11:59:59 pm: commit, push, then open the commit on your repo's GitHub page,
   copy its URL, and paste it into the Problem Set 1 assignment in Canvas.

## Get GitHub student benefits {#student-benefits}

GitHub Education is free for students. It gives you GitHub Pro, which raises your free
Codespaces time from about 60 to about 90 hours a month, and GitHub Copilot Student. You
don't need it to start: your codespace works while your application is reviewed.

The **Join GitHub Education** button on [education.github.com](https://education.github.com)
leads to the same application as the steps below.

1. **Add your WSU email first.** On GitHub, click your profile picture (top right) >
   **Settings** > **Emails**. Add your `@wsu.edu` address, then click the link in the
   email GitHub sends you to verify it.
2. **Check your name.** Under **Settings** > **Public profile**, put your real first and
   last name in **Name**, as it appears on your WSU documents. (Your *username* can still be
   anything.) If GitHub asks for billing information during the application, use the same
   name. Nothing is charged.
3. **Start the application.** Go to
   [github.com/settings/education/benefits](https://github.com/settings/education/benefits)
   (or **Settings** > **Education benefits**) and click **Start an application**.
4. **Fill it in.** Choose **Student**, select **Washington State University**, and pick your
   `@wsu.edu` email.
5. **Show proof that you're enrolled,** if asked. GitHub asks you to take a photo with your
   camera rather than upload a file. Use a document that shows your full name,
   "Washington State University", and a current date, such as your class schedule or
   an enrollment verification from myWSU. A Cougar Card works only if it shows a current
   date. Photographing the document on a screen or on paper is fine, as long as it's sharp.
6. **Submit.** For the best chance, apply on campus with your browser allowed to share
   your location, and with any VPN turned off.
7. **Wait for two emails.** Approval usually takes a few days, longer at the start of a
   semester. The benefits themselves can take up to 3 more days to appear. You can check
   the status on the same
   [Education benefits](https://github.com/settings/education/benefits) page.

**If you're turned down,** the email says why, most often a name that doesn't match or a
blurry or undated document. Fix that one thing, then apply again with a new photo.

**Copilot:** once you're approved, you can turn on Copilot Student from the same Education
benefits page. In course codespaces, Copilot's autocomplete stays off through Week 5
(see [Policies](policies.qmd)); Copilot Chat is fine to use.

## Each time you work {#each-time}

- **Open your codespace:** your repo's page > **Code** > **Codespaces** tab >
  click the codespace that's already there. Reuse it; don't create a new one
  each time.
- **Start by pulling:** in Source Control, click **Sync Changes** (or **⋯ > Pull**)
  so you have any new problem sets.
- **Before you leave: commit and push.** Your work is only safe once it's on
  GitHub. A codespace you stop using for a few weeks is deleted, and anything
  not pushed goes with it.
- **Then close the tab.** The codespace stops by itself after 30 idle minutes.
  To stop it right away, go to [github.com/codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces),
  click **⋯** next to it, and choose **Stop codespace**.
- **On a lab or shared computer,** sign out of GitHub when you're done.

**Your monthly allowance:** your GitHub account includes about 60 hours of
codespace time a month, or 90 once your student benefits are approved. That's
plenty for this course if you stop your codespace when you're done. You can see
your usage under **Settings > Billing** on GitHub.

## Every problem set and lab

Problem sets and labs arrive in your repo as folders numbered by week: Week 4 brings
`probset04/` (Problem Set 4) and `lab04/` (Lab 4). A week without one skips its number.

1. **Pull** (Source Control > **Sync Changes**). The new `probsetNN/` or `labNN/` folder appears.
2. **Work** in the notebook inside it (`probsetNN/probsetNN.ipynb` or `labNN/labNN.ipynb`),
   and commit whenever something works.
3. **Labs:** commit and push (Sync Changes) before class ends. There is nothing to
   submit in Canvas.
4. **Problem sets:** click **Restart**, then **Run All**. If it doesn't run from top to
   bottom, it isn't finished. Fill in the **AI usage note** at the bottom.
5. **Problem sets:** commit, push (Sync Changes), **copy the commit URL** from GitHub,
   and **paste it into Canvas** before the deadline.

## Rules of the road {#rules}

- Your repo is private. Never make it public or share it, even after the course,
  unless an assignment says it may be shared.
- Use relative paths (`data/prices.csv`), never full paths like `C:\Users\...`
  or `/workspaces/...`. Your code must run on the instructor's machine.
- Don't commit `.venv/` or big data files. GitHub rejects files over 100 MB, and
  your repo's `.gitignore` handles the common cases.
- Don't change `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock`. If you think you need another
  package, ask on Discussions.
- **Asking for help:** see [Getting help](setup-faq.qmd#getting-help).
